(1953, 91m) dir Anthony Mann w/James Stewart, Janet Leigh, Robert Ryan. “By the time Anthony Mann and James Stewart made The Naked Spur in 1953, they’d set the formula for their Westerns: man with shady past involves himself in righting a moral situation while maybe not being entirely moral and forthright himself. In this, my favorite of the five, you toss in Janet Leigh, some Robert Ryan, a little Ralph Meeker (there are only five speaking parts!) and you have one of the most taut films the world knows.” —Ted Harwood, Trylon volunteer since 2016

(1943, 97m, Danish w/English subtitles) dir Carl Theodor Dreyer w/Lisbeth Movin, Sigrid Neiiendam, Thorkild Roose. Young and unhappily married Anne (Movin) is thrown into turmoil as local deacons, including her elderly husband (Roose), accuse her neighbors of witchcraft. When she falls in love with her stepson, she treads in dangerous waters. Made during the Nazi occupation of Denmark, Day of Wrath is a brilliant tale of accusation and persecution.
